title: Can convincing samples miss a mode?
hook: Compare detector loss with distribution coverage.

doesNotKnow: Real A/B=.5/.5; D(A)=D(B)=.9. Does equal generator loss prove both modes appear?

objective: Compute this finite gan-mode-collapse model, compare earned countercases, and explain its stated boundary.

claims.text:
gan-mode-collapse

**Identity / target / source:** `ai:gan-mode-collapse` → `ai-gan-mode-collapse` → `src/demos/ai/ai-gan-mode-collapse`; source `company/domains/proposals/2026-10-18-ai-map-expansion.json#concepts/79`; brief `company/domains/briefs/2026-10-19-ai-next30e.md#2-gan-mode-collapse`. **Packet:** G1. **Level / prerequisites:** core; `ai:gan-forger-detective`.

**Nearest / distinct payoff:** gan-forger-detective updates a game; here a limited discriminator cannot distinguish mode coverage even when samples receive equal realism scores.

**Computed primary model:** Real distribution p(A)=p(B)=.5. Fixed limited discriminatorD(A)=D(B)=.9. Collapsed generatorq=[1,0] and coveringq=[.5,.5] both have non-saturating loss−ln.9≈.10536. Their covered real modes are1/2 versus2/2, and total-variation distances fromp are.5 versus0.

**Countercase / boundary:** An ideal density-ratio discriminator recomputed for eachq has D_i=p_i/(p_i+q_i). Against collapsed q its generator lossln3; against coveringq it isln2. Equal loss under the limited detector therefore does not establish distributional equality. Ignore q_i=0 loss terms using0log conventions; do not take log0 unnecessarily.

**Prediction / transfer recall:** Predict whether matching the limited detector’s score proves both modes are represented; recall a third valid mode unseen by that detector would require its own coverage check.

**Intervention / retained witness:** Toggle collapse/cover computes mass bars, detector loss, coverage and TV; Upgrade detector recomputes density ratios, retaining original equal-loss counterexample. No promise that actual alternating training finds the ideal discriminator.

**Source obligation:** [Goodfellow et al. original PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1406.2661), opened2026-10-19, §3 Eq1, non-saturating generator alternative and Algorithm1 (PDFpp3–4), §4.1 optimal discriminator. These explicit finite gradients/limited classifiers are local derivations, not the paper’s image experiments or a convergence claim.
